_comment: Works withheld because they are still in copyright in Germany, where the site is operated. Keyed '<folder>/<filename>'. Read by scripts/lib/takedowns.mjs: build-data never catalogues these, shrink never encodes them, the Commons fetch never writes sidecar entries for them, and assets:sync refuses to run while a variant dir for one exists. The originals are kept in assets/.rejected/copyright/ and their variants in assets/.rejected/copyright-variants/, neither of which is read or synced, so a work can be restored once its term ends: remove its entry here, move both back, then run assets:shrink, assets:build-data and assets:sync. 'publicDomainInGermanyFrom' is informational and nothing acts on it automatically. Works whose status depends on the EU rule of the shorter term (Kawase Hasui, Kawai Gyokudō, Pu Xian, Pu Ru and others) are deliberately NOT listed; that is an open legal question. See metadata/copyright-takedown-2026-09.md.

With a 2013 Christie's HK sale (sale 3211, lot 1410) and a contemporary cloud-sea style, 2013 is the likely year. That would put it in copyright whatever the death year. The 1953 reading cannot be excluded, and I found no death year for the painter, so the verdict stays unidentified. It must not be treated as public domain.

collection-of-beauty/a9d3e89a-7152-4bc2-.note: I agree to keep it off public domain. This is a small 310x800 ink landscape in Huang Binhong's manner, with a signature too blurred to read reliably and no provenance. If the work is genuine, Huang died in 1955 and it would be public domain. But his work is heavily forged, and a later imitator could still be in copyright.

collection-of-beauty/_L'homme_est_en_mer.artist: Unknown modern copyist (reproduction after Vincent van Gogh, after Virginie Demont-Breton)
collection-of-beauty/_L'homme_est_en_mer.note: Changed. This image is not Van Gogh's 1889 canvas. The preview carries a 'PaintingMania.com' watermark at top left and bottom right, and that site sells hand-painted oil reproductions. The brushwork is cruder than the original, so this is a photo of a recent commercial copy. The metadata also says the file was 'Not found on Wikimedia Commons'. The underlying composition is public domain (Van Gogh d.1890, Demont-Breton d.1935 per Wikidata Q3560732), and a slavish copy probably has no new copyright in Germany. But the object is a modern work by an unknown maker, taken from a commercial site that asserts rights with a watermark, so it should not be treated as clearly public domain. Replace it with a photograph of the real painting.

collection-of-beauty/H22611-L388076506_o.note: Changed from public_domain. The work has no sidecar, no traceable sale and no catalogue attribution. The only link to Huang Binhong (d. 1955) is the signature 賓虹 and seal on a loosely brushed scroll. Huang Binhong is among the most forged Chinese painters, and a later hand would still be in copyright. A signature alone does not meet the sourced-attribution bar for public_domain, so this should stay offline until the lot is traced.

collection-of-beauty/2013_HGK_03211_1118.note: I agree it must not be called public domain. Zoomed in, the inscription reads 霜秋十渡柿紅圖 王然寫生: a sketch from life at Shidu near Beijing, with a seal naming him a disciple of '少梁先生'. That points to a 20th-century, probably living or recently deceased painter. I found no authoritative life dates, and he may well be in copyright.
